subject: history_social
passage: A hoard of coins cannot have been buried before its most recent coin was made, but it could have been buried long afterward, so archaeologists look for further clues. One such clue is wear: coins lose detail steadily as they pass from hand to hand. A hoard of 1,400 Roman silver coins found in a field in what is now France contained coins made over a span of about sixty years, the latest in 268 CE. Numismatist Claire Fontaine found that the latest coins were nearly as crisp as when they left the mint, while older coins in the same hoard were heavily worn. These observations suggest that the hoard was ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: hidden by a soldier who was fleeing from an invading army in the year 268 CE.
choices.B: buried several decades after 268 CE, once even the newest coins had begun to wear.
choices.C: buried some years before 268 CE by a person who had collected coins for decades.
choices.D: most likely buried within a few years after the latest coins were made in 268 CE.

explanation.why: The latest coin sets the earliest possible burial date, 268 CE. Wear shows how long coins circulated: the newest coins were almost unworn, so they had spent little time in use before burial. Together, the clues point to burial soon after 268 CE.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text gives no information about who buried the hoard or why.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The newest coins were nearly crisp, which suggests a short time in circulation, not decades.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says a hoard cannot be buried before its most recent coin was made.
explanation.D: Correct. The earliest possible date (268 CE) plus the nearly unworn newest coins point to burial soon after that date.
